newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities steady to higher.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended steady to slightly higher in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Thursday.
"The market was mixed because of the month-end factor. The morning session was quiet but the market closed unchanged as at yesterday's levels," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months was unchanged from Wednesday's yield of 2.80/2.75 percent and one-year unchanged at a yield at 2.83/2.78 percent.

Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.55/98.60 compared with Wednesday's close of S$98.48/98.53, September 2001 at S$96.30/96.40 against S$96.25/96.35 and June 2003 at S$94.15/94.20 from S$94.13/94.18.
The overnight interbank offered rate was unchanged from Wednesday's 4 3-7/8 percent.
